chapter: Hampton and Basie: tours and road life
title: Touring rushed; seeing countries on later visits
summary: First tours are fast, with later visits letting him study how people live and their economies.

story.theme_name: Going abroad: American jazz musicians touring and living in Europe
story.community_name: Going abroad: touring Europe and Japan

blocks.x: On your tours with the other countries, were they always so vast that you didn't have a chance to (inaudible)?

Sometimes they're very fast. It's always that way your first time around. I would say, it's usually that way your first time around. When you really get to the place where you can enjoy countries, it's when you have a chance to make it your second or third time around because then you can program yourself and you know what you want to see and how you want to see and why you want to see it.
You don't very often have days off though, do you?
Very seldom. That's why it takes you

two or three times around to really get yourself accustomed to what you want to see as part of that country's culture. I like to get down to the inside of a country. I like to find out how they go to the store and what they shop for and what their monetary value is, in comparison to what ours is and what their basis of economy is and actually, how the lower class, middle class or upper class are, in some countries, they only have a lower class and a upper class. I like to learn the classes of the people and how they are accepted by their governments and what they do and why and how and how they live, their means of survival and how their homes are located and their transportations and the amount of money that the country is based on as a medium for the average man's earnings and just what the world's built on, the stock exchange of their country.
